images.caption: Afghan Minister of Interior Bismillah Khan Mohammadi, center, cuts a ribbon symbolizing the opening of the Afghan National Civil Order Police headquarters and stand up of the 5th Brigade at Lashkar Gah in the Helmand Province, Afghanistan, July 25, 2011. The minister was joined by the ANCOP and provincial police commanders, Provincial government leaders and elders and the Governor of Helmand, Gulab Mangal (far right). The headquarters opening and brigade standup come one week after the Afghans took over security control in the Helmand Province from coalition forces. (U.S. photo by Senior Airman Kat Lynn Justen)
images.alt: Afghan Minister of Interior Bismillah Khan Mohammadi, center, cuts a ribbon symbolizing the opening of the Afghan National Civil Order Police headquarters and stand up of the 5th Brigade at Lashkar Gah in the Helmand Province, Afghanistan, July 25, 2011. The minister was joined by the ANCOP and provincial police commanders, Provincial government leaders and elders and the Governor of Helmand, Gulab Mangal (far right). The headquarters opening and brigade standup come one week after the Afghans took over security control in the Helmand Province from coalition forces. (U.S. photo by Senior Airman Kat Lynn Justen)

images.caption: U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Joseph Nunez and Viky, a Marine Corps improvised explosive device detector dog, both attached to Fox Company, 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marine Regiment, search a compound for hidden threats during Operation Grizzly in Helmand province, Afghanistan, July 18, 2013. Grizzly was a counterinsurgency operation to deter enemy activity, establish a presence and gather intelligence. (DoD photo by Cpl. Alejandro Pena, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

images.caption: U.S. Navy Construction Mechanic 3rd Class Cody A. Brown, assigned to Naval Mobile Construction Battalion (NMCB) 11, removes a drive shaft on a mine-resistant, ambush-protected vehicle in Helmand province, Afghanistan, June 15, 2012.  NMCB-11 was deployed to Afghanistan to conduct general, mobility and survivability engineering operations, defensive operations, Afghan National Army partnering and detachment of units in order to enable the neutralization of insurgency and support improved governance and stability operations. (DoD photo by Construction Mechanic 2nd Class Brandon Trumbo, U.S. Navy/Released)

images.caption: U.S. Marine Corps Lieutenant Col. Sean Riordan, left, the commanding officer of 1st Battalion, 3rd Marine Regiment; and British Army Brigadier Nicholas Welch, right, the deputy commander of Regional Command Southwest (RC (SW)), greet an Afghan agricultural specialist as they walk through a marketplace outside Forward Operating Base Delhi in Garmsir, Afghanistan, June 16, 2011. Welch traveled from Camp Leatherneck, Afghanistan, with other military leaders from RC (SW) to perform a district deep-dive, a forum to explain in-depth information in each district the U.S. Marines represent, and to discuss progress and issues in the Garmsir District area of operations. (DoD photo by Sgt. Mallory S. VanderSchans, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)
